clue.text: Camus's 28

parts.note: 28 across is a nonconformist; Camus wrote a long essay, L'Homme révolté, whose English title names such a figure

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another answer, as written by Albert Camus.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 across is DISSENTER; Camus's book-length essay L'Homme révolté is known in English by a word meaning the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Camus's essay title in English is a synonym of nonconformist, the sense of 28 across.

clue.text: Reader, she married him

parts.note: twists the famous line 'Reader, I married him' from Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre into the third person

explanation.surface: An address to the reader about a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Eyre's closing chapter opens 'Reader, I married him'; the clue asks whom she married, the master of Thornfield Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre's husband at the novel's end is Edward Fairfax Rochester.

clue.text: His dream was Murdoch's

parts.note: Iris Murdoch wrote a 1969 novel titled after one man's dream

explanation.surface: Someone's dream turns out to belong to Murdoch.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris Murdoch's novel Bruno's Dream (1969) centres on a dying old man.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Iris Murdoch's novel is the dreamer named in the book's title.

clue.text: Robber bridgegroom said to secure deer

parts.note: to secure a door is to lock it
a hart is a male deer

explanation.surface: A thieving groom is reported to fasten a stag.
explanation.walkthrough: In Eudora Welty's novella The Robber Bridegroom the title character is Jamie Lockhart; 'said to' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie Lockhart is the bandit hero of Eudora Welty's The Robber Bridegroom.

clue.text: Visit clue revision for old law book

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone revises a crossword clue about a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges VISITCLUE into the book of the Pentateuch.
explanation.definitionFit: The third book of the Old Testament sets out the Mosaic laws for priests and worship.

clue.text: Gaskell witch-a product of the soil

indicators.note: what is produced from the soil is the same letters worked into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A witch from Mrs Gaskell's fiction grown out of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a product of the' rearranges SOIL; Elizabeth Gaskell's story Lois the Witch is set during the Salem trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaskell's novella Lois the Witch names its heroine in its title.

clue.text: Mayfair expos bodes evil, I stir it up

indicators.note: stirring things up mixes them, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An exposé of high society portends trouble, and the writer stirs it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir it up' rearranges BODESEVILI into the title of Evelyn Waugh's 1930 satire on Mayfair's Bright Young Things; 'expos' is the OCR form of exposé.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's Vile Bodies satirises the fashionable young set of London's smart Mayfair district.

clue.text: El Greco's home looted, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the word looted could be another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Was the painter's house ransacked?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges LOOTED into the Spanish city where El Greco lived and painted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born painter El Greco settled in the Castilian city on the Tagus in 1577.

clue.text: Press historian

definitions.meaning: the Oxford University Press printing house was long known by the name of the building it occupied
Edward Hyde, 1st Earl, wrote The History of the Rebellion

explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's printing house was named after the Earl's building, and the Earl himself chronicled the English Civil War.

clue.text: A broadside from Waldo Frank?

parts.note: the American critic Waldo Frank published a 1924 collection of critical pieces whose title is the plural of a word for a volley of fire

explanation.surface: The American writer Waldo Frank lets fly with an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Waldo Frank's book of essays on books and plays was titled Salvos; one of them is a single broadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a simultaneous discharge of guns, and the word extends to a burst of criticism.

clue.text: War correspondent who developed other talents, winning Nobel Prize for literature

definitions.text: War correspondent who developed other talents, winning Nobel Prize for literature

parts.words: War correspondent who developed other talents, winning Nobel Prize for literature
parts.note: describes a reporter of the Boer War who became a statesman and won the 1953 literature prize

explanation.surface: A career sketch of a journalist turned many-sided Nobel laureate.
explanation.walkthrough: He reported from Cuba and the Boer War before politics; the 1953 Nobel Prize in Literature honoured his histories and speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was a war correspondent in South Africa and later a Nobel literature laureate.

clue.text: Thriller writer in nearly all bestseller lists

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the clue's own words nearly all

explanation.surface: A thriller author features in almost every bestseller list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run inside 'nearLY ALL', the surname of the British thriller writer Gavin Lyall; 'bestseller lists' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavin Lyall wrote aviation and spy thrillers such as The Wrong Side of the Sky.

clue.text: Strauss's baron on record for long periods

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
Baron Ochs is the boorish nobleman in Richard Strauss's opera Der Rosenkavalier

explanation.surface: An opera character appears on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: Baron Ochs auf Lerchenau is the comic villain of Der Rosenkavalier.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long spans of history, the same as ages.

clue.text: The Gentleman was not for burning

definitions.text: The Gentleman was not for burning

parts.words: The Gentleman was not for burning
parts.note: plays on Christopher Fry's title The Lady's Not for Burning, pointing to a man from the Book of Daniel who survived the fiery furnace

explanation.surface: A man version of Christopher Fry's comedy The Lady's Not for Burning.
explanation.walkthrough: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were thrown into Nebuchadnezzar's furnace and came out unharmed (Daniel 3).
explanation.definitionFit: One of the three Hebrews in Daniel survived the furnace, so fire would not burn him.

clue.text: Unofficial centre of Viertel's Huston type,

parts.note: a black market is unofficial trading
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: The unofficial core of Peter Viertel's portrait of John Huston.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Viertel's novel White Hunter, Black Heart portrays a director modelled on John Huston; the clue's trailing comma is as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Viertel's title labels the Huston figure as a cruel, wicked character.

clue.text: Introduction by Wordsworth-or one of several by Alice Meynell

definitions.meaning: Wordsworth's long autobiographical poem was meant as an introductory piece to a larger work

definitions.text: one of several by Alice Meynell
definitions.meaning: Alice Meynell's first collection was titled Preludes, so one poem from it

explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's autobiographical poem is a preface by name, and Meynell's 1875 book Preludes contained several such pieces.

clue.text: Sort of heroines Jane Eyre and Lady Windermere were

definitions.text: Sort of heroines Jane Eyre and Lady Windermere were

parts.words: Sort of heroines Jane Eyre and Lady Windermere were
parts.note: both women give their names to the works they appear in, Jane Eyre and Lady Windermere's Fan

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of heroine two classic women share.
explanation.walkthrough: Brontë's novel and Wilde's play Lady Windermere's Fan are both named after their heroines.
explanation.definitionFit: A character who gives a work its title is described as title-giving in this sense.

clue.text: First of Dryden's early significant poems

indicators.note: First tells us to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Dryden's first major early verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' takes the initials of 'of Dryden's early significant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject are a classic verse form Dryden himself wrote.

clue.text: Road to balanced odds on successful writer

parts.note: ST is short for street, a road
evens is betting odds of one to one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipster's route to even money on a winning author.
explanation.walkthrough: Evens is a bookmaker's term for odds where the stake equals the possible win.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a best-selling author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Every intellectual is latently political (Thomas Mann)

definitions.text: Every intellectual is latently political (Thomas Mann)

parts.words: Every intellectual is latently political (Thomas Mann)
parts.note: a quotation from Thomas Mann with one word missing after intellectual

explanation.surface: A Thomas Mann aphorism about thought and politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Mann's line runs 'Every intellectual attitude is latently political'; the solver fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Mann's saying is a noun meaning a stance or outlook.

clue.text: Was Joe Lampton's the penthouse?

parts.note: Joe Lampton is the ambitious hero of John Braine's novel ... at the Top, and a penthouse is the top flat

explanation.surface: A question about where John Braine's social climber lived.
explanation.walkthrough: John Braine's 1957 novel Room at the Top follows Joe Lampton's climb up the social ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is literally lodging at the top, echoing Braine's title.

clue.text: Resignation in Powell's world

definitions.meaning: resignation is quiet submission to what cannot be changed
Anthony Powell's novel The ... World is the third volume of A Dance to the Music of Time

explanation.definitionFit: Resignation means submission, and Powell named a novel after the financial world of bills of exchange.

clue.text: Barrie villain quietly furious

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
irate means furious

explanation.surface: A villain from J. M. Barrie's work fumes in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Hook of Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's most famous villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrie's Captain Hook commands a crew of sea-robbers on the Jolly Roger.

clue.text: All the long and lone—/Thou wovest dreams of joy and fear "(Shelley)

definitions.text: All the long and lone—/Thou wovest dreams of joy and fear "(Shelley)

parts.words: All the long and lone—/Thou wovest dreams of joy and fear "(Shelley)
parts.note: lines from Shelley's To Night with the last word of the first line left out

explanation.surface: Two lines from Shelley's poem To Night with a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley's To Night reads 'all the long and lone daylight, / Thou wovest dreams of joy and fear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Shelley's line names the hours when the sun is up.

clue.text: E.F. Benson's king of Kings?

parts.note: E. F. Benson wrote ... of King's, about a student at King's College, Cambridge, and the Bible's king shares the name

explanation.surface: E. F. Benson's monarch of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: Benson's novel David of King's is set at King's College, Cambridge; the biblical king of Israel bears the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Benson's hero shares his name with the shepherd who became king of Israel.

clue.text: Material introduction to Adrian's Miss Townsend

indicators.note: an introduction is a beginning, so the opening letter of to is taken

parts.note: the 's of Adrian's stands for is
Sue Townsend is the author of the Adrian Mole diaries

explanation.surface: The opening of Adrian Mole's diaries, introducing Sue Townsend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction' takes the T of 'to'; Adrian Mole is Sue Townsend's diarist, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine fabric, such as gauze, is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Kate, the domesticated insectivore

definitions.meaning: Katherina in Shakespeare's The Taming of the ... is a scold
a small mouse-like insect-eating mammal, here tamed as in Shakespeare's title

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Kate is a scolding woman, and the same word names a small insect-eating mammal.

clue.text: Lawrence's sainted equine — you could be getting warm

indicators.note: could be getting signals that the word warm may turn into another arrangement

explanation.surface: D. H. Lawrence's holy horse; you might be closing in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be getting' rearranges WARM; D. H. Lawrence's novella St Mawr is named after a stallion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence's St Mawr is a bay stallion, the saint in his name.

clue.text: Conrad's Italian patriot is instrumental

definitions.meaning: Giorgio ... is the old Garibaldino in Joseph Conrad's Nostromo
adjective standing for a member of the violin family, a musical instrument

explanation.definitionFit: Conrad's Garibaldi veteran in Nostromo shares his surname with the stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin.

clue.text: Hues and auras blended in Persian king

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Colours and glows mingle in a Persian monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' rearranges HUESAURAS into the king of the Book of Esther.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahasuerus is the Persian ruler who marries Esther in the Bible.

clue.text: Defoe offered a very short way with him

definitions.text: Defoe offered a very short way with him

parts.words: Defoe offered a very short way with him
parts.note: Defoe's satirical pamphlet The Shortest Way with the ...

explanation.surface: Defoe proposed swift treatment for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Defoe's 1702 pamphlet The Shortest Way with the Dissenters ironically urged harsh suppression of nonconformists.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's pamphlet title names a Protestant nonconformist outside the Church of England.

clue.text: Dickensian mystery man

parts.note: Dickens left The Mystery of ... Drood unfinished, its title character vanishing

explanation.surface: A puzzling character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens died before finishing The Mystery of Edwin Drood, so the young man's fate is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Drood, the title character of Dickens's last unfinished novel, is the man at the heart of the mystery.
